#2 The standard derivation of the Thom iso via a “relative” Serre spectral sequence for a “relative fibration” feels a little inefficient. There should be a way to use just a plain Serre spectral sequence for a plain Serre fibration.

Let me see:

Given a vector bundle V→XV \to XV→X of rank nnn, let me write

E≔D(V)/BS(V) E \coloneqq D(V)/_{B} S(V) E:=D(V)/B​S(V)

for the fiberwise quotient, an nnn-sphere bundle over XXX

Sn−1↪Dn⟶Sn↓↓↓S(V)↪D(V)⟶E↓↓↓B=B=B \begin{matrix} S^{n-1} &\hookrightarrow& D^n &\longrightarrow& S^n \\ \downarrow && \downarrow && \downarrow \\ S(V) &\hookrightarrow& D(V) &\longrightarrow& E \\ \downarrow && \downarrow && \downarrow \\ B &=& B &=& B \end{matrix} Sn−1↓S(V)↓B​↪↪=​Dn↓D(V)↓B​⟶⟶=​Sn↓E↓B​

This way the reduced cohomology of the Thom space is the relative cohomology fo EEE relative BBB:

H~∙(Th(V))≃H∙(E,B) . \tilde H^\bullet(\mathrm{Th}(V)) \simeq H^\bullet(E,B) \,. H~∙(Th(V))≃H∙(E,B).

Moreover, this EEE has a section.

Therefore combining the exact sequence in unreduced relative cohomology (horizontally) with the Thom-Gysin sequence (vertically) gives

H∙(B)↓↘≃H∙(E,B)⟶H∙(E)⟶H∙(B)↓H∙−n(B) . \begin{matrix} && H^\bullet(B) \\ && \downarrow & \searrow^{\mathrlap{\simeq}} \\ H^\bullet(E,B) &\longrightarrow& H^\bullet(E) &\longrightarrow& H^\bullet(B) \\ && \downarrow \\ && H^{\bullet-n}(B) \end{matrix} \,. H∙(E,B)​⟶​H∙(B)↓H∙(E)↓H∙−n(B)​↘≃⟶​H∙(B)​.

By the iso in the top right (from the section of EEE) there is a splitting of the horizontal sequence

H∙(E)≃H∙(E,B)⊕H∙(B)≃H~∙(Th(V))⊕H∙(B) \begin{aligned} H^\bullet(E) & \simeq H^\bullet(E,B) \oplus H^\bullet(B) \\ & \simeq \tilde H^\bullet(\mathrm{Th}(V)) \oplus H^\bullet(B) \end{aligned} H∙(E)​≃H∙(E,B)⊕H∙(B)≃H~∙(Th(V))⊕H∙(B)​

but this then implies from exactness of the vertical sequence an iso

H~∙(Th(V))⟶≃H∙−n(B) . \tilde H^\bullet(\mathrm{Th}(V)) \overset{\simeq}{\longrightarrow} H^{\bullet-n}(B) \,. H~∙(Th(V))⟶≃​H∙−n(B).

That should be the Thom isomorphism, no?

#4 The argument in Kochmann 96, prop. 4.3.6 for the EEE-Thom isomorphism in generalized EEE-cohomology has an elegant strategy: argue that the operation of pullback followed by cup product with the EEE-Thom class induces on the second page of the respective relative EEE-Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequences the Thom isomorphism with an induced orientation class in ordinary cohomology with coefficients in π0(E)\pi_0(E)π0​(E).

But I feel dubious about Kochmann’s argument as to why this holds. Even if his argument holds water, it relies, he says, on the assumption that π0(E)\pi_0(E)π0​(E) is cyclic, which is an assumption that shouldn’t be there.

I am thinking an argument should go as follows: since the Thom space of a rank nnn vector bundles has vanishing ordinary cohomology in degrees <n\lt n<n, the relative Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence gives an isomorphism

Hn(D(V),S(V);π0(E))≃En(D(V),S(V)) H^n(D(V),S(V); \pi_0(E)) \simeq E^n(D(V), S(V)) Hn(D(V),S(V);π0​(E))≃En(D(V),S(V))

and under that iso orientations should go to orientations.

Is there any textbook (or similar) that would use this approach to the EEE-Thom isomorphism?
